title: The ORB Framework: Owned, Rented, and Borrowed audiences as a marketing strategy
summary: Corey Haines breaks every marketing channel into Owned, Rented, or Borrowed lines of communication to an audience. Owned platforms are the priority, rented ones add discovery but carry platform risk, and borrowed audiences are the under-used way to kickstart growth on the other two.

principles.text: Sort every channel as Owned, Rented, or Borrowed, and point everything back to owned platforms.
principles.quote: I've found that marketing strategies and tactics can be broken down into three main categories: **Owned**, **Rented**, and **Borrowed**.

principles.text: Owned platforms are the priority: you own the line of communication, and they get more effective over time.
principles.quote: Naturally, owned platforms get more effective over time whereas borrowed and rented platforms usually get less effective over time.

principles.text: Pick only one or two owned platforms at the intersection of what you love doing and what your audience wants.
principles.quote: Find the intersection between what you love doing and what your audience wants.

principles.text: Use rented platforms for discovery, but commit to a few rather than being everywhere.
principles.quote: Meet your audience where they already are. Commit to a few — you don't have to have a strategy for every single rented platform.

principles.text: Borrow other people's audiences actively, not passively, to kickstart growth on owned and rented platforms.
principles.quote: Borrowing other people's audience is the key to kickstarting your growth on owned and rented platforms.

principles.text: To borrow well, list everyone who holds your audience's attention and craft a win-win collaboration; start by asking your audience.
principles.quote: Make a list of everyone and everything that has the attention of your intended audience.
